# pygate-ci

Deterministic Python quality gate CLI.

Use this repo when you need to:
- combine Ruff, Pyright, and pytest into one gate result
- produce structured escalation artifacts for CI or agents
- attempt bounded deterministic repair before handing work off

Primary CLI:
- `pygate run --mode canary --changed-files <path>`
- `pygate summarize --input <failures.json>`
- `pygate repair --input <failures.json>`

Agent skill (portable Agent Plugin at the repo root):
- canonical skill: `skills/quick-gate-python/SKILL.md`
- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add hermes-labs-ai/quick-gate-python`, then `claude plugin install quick-gate-python@quick-gate-python`
- Codex CLI: `codex plugin marketplace add hermes-labs-ai/quick-gate-python`, then `codex plugin add quick-gate-python@quick-gate-python`
- Gemini CLI: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/quick-gate-python --ref main`

Pre-commit hook (native `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, pinned to an immutable commit):
- `repo: https://github.com/hermes-labs-ai/quick-gate-python`, `rev: 00e561917dd1772252773aef060c07c2b8719377`
- `id: pygate` runs canary mode (Ruff + Pyright); `id: pygate-full` adds pytest
- the hook environment is isolated and installs the pinned gate tools itself; pygate's own
  install carries runtime dependencies only
- full mode's project test dependencies stay caller-owned, and a consumer's
  `additional_dependencies` replaces the manifest list rather than extending it

Root GitHub Action quickstart (audited immutable commit):
- `hermes-labs-ai/quick-gate-python@aef81b5e832f98aaef02b0a1f64f8eed277e92f1`
- grant `contents: read` only for the blocking read-only baseline
- use `mode: canary`, `fail-on-error: "true"`, and leave repair/comments disabled
- `v0.2.1` is the first release tag that contains the root `action.yml` and is a valid convenience
  reference; earlier tags do not resolve as an action reference
- pin the audited commit for an immutable supply-chain reference; never use a mutable branch reference

Root action inputs:
- `mode`, `repair`, `max-attempts`, `python-version`, `post-comment`
- `changed-files`, `artifact-name`, `fail-on-error`

Root action outputs:
- `status`: final `pass`, `fail`, or `escalated`
- `gate-status`: raw initial `pass` or `fail`
- `repair-status`: `pass`, `escalated`, or `skipped`
- `full-mode-dependency-status`: `ready`, `missing`, or `not-required`
- `full-mode-dependency-classification`, `changed-files-strategy`, `failures-json`

Full mode is caller-owned: install project dependencies plus `pytest` and `pytest-json-report` before the action step in the selected Python environment. The action uploads hidden `.pygate/` evidence files under `artifact-name` (default `pygate-artifacts`). Repair is opt-in and can mutate eligible consumer files; comments are opt-in and require `pull-requests: write`, which is commonly unavailable for fork-origin pull requests.

Outputs:
- failures, run metadata, repair report, escalation, and agent-brief artifacts under `.pygate/`

Do not use this repo as:
- a generic lint aggregator
- a semantic code-fix engine
- a replacement for the underlying tools and their own configuration

Key success condition:
- the same gate outputs produce the same normalized artifacts and escalation decisions
